entry: Infinite sum of terms expressed through a function's [[Derivative|derivatives]] at a single point. For most common functions, the function and its Taylor series are equal near that point. Brook Taylor introduced the series in 1715; when the point is 0, it is called a Maclaurin series, after Colin Maclaurin, who made extensive use of this case in the 18th century. The first n + 1 terms form the nth Taylor polynomial, a [[Polynomial|polynomial]] of degree n that generally becomes more accurate as n increases. Taylor's theorem estimates the error of such approximations. A function is analytic at a point if it equals the sum of its Taylor series on an open interval containing that point. Taylor series can be differentiated and integrated term by term, and they combine algebraically through sums, products and compositions. Standard Maclaurin series serve as starting points for computing others.

Capital and largest city of [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]]. With more than 1.3 million inhabitants, it contains almost one third of the country's population. Vakhtang I of Iberia founded the city in the 5th century CE, and it has since served as the capital of various Georgian kingdoms and republics. From 1801 to 1917, then part of the [[Russian Empire]], it was the seat of the Caucasus Viceroyalty. Its location at the crossroads of Europe and Asia, near the [[Silk Road]], has made it a point of contention among global powers. Its architecture mixes medieval, neoclassical, [[Art Nouveau]], Stalinist and modern styles. Notable sites include the Sameba and Sioni cathedrals, Freedom Square and the medieval Narikala Fortress. The name derives from the Georgian word for "warm," reflecting the city's [[Hot spring|hot springs]]. Summer temperatures mostly range from 20 to 32 °C (68 to 90 °F).

Person who helps students acquire knowledge, competence or virtue through [[Teaching|teaching]]. Teachers are also called schoolteachers or educators. Anyone may take on the role informally, but in most countries formal teaching in [[School|schools]] and colleges is done by paid professionals. Duties include preparing lessons according to agreed [[Curriculum|curricula]], giving lessons and assessing pupil progress. Teachers may instruct in [[Literacy|literacy]] and numeracy, vocational skills, the [[The arts|arts]], religion, civics or life skills. They have a legal duty to protect students from harm, such as bullying and abuse. The required competences vary by culture, and the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development has argued for a shared definition of what teachers need to know and do.

Practice by which a [[Teacher|teacher]] transmits skills, including knowledge, know-how and interpersonal skills, to a learner or other audience. Teaching is closely related to [[Learning|learning]], the student's activity of absorbing that knowledge, and it forms part of the broader concept of [[Education|education]]. In psychology, teaching is often defined by the teacher's intent to help others learn. Children show teaching abilities early: as young as twelve months, they help adults find an object when the adult shows ignorance of its location, and by age four they prefer to transmit true information. Caro and Hauser proposed a functional definition for animals: a behavior counts as teaching if it occurs only in the presence of a naive individual, costs the teacher or gives no direct benefit, and produces a learning gain in the learner.

Dark [[Cyan|cyan]] color named after the Eurasian teal duck. It can be made by mixing cyan with black or gray, and it is one of the first 16 HTML/CSS [[Web colors|web colors]]. On screens, teal is cyan with about half its brightness. The first recorded use of teal as an English color name was in 1917. In [[North America]] it became a fad color in the 1990s, and many sports teams adopted it. Teal is the official color of the [[Kochi]] Metro in India, and the jersey color of the [[Belfast]] Giants ice hockey team.

Political corruption scandal in the [[United States]] during the Harding administration. Secretary of the Interior Albert B. Fall accepted bribes from private oil companies to lease naval [[Petroleum|petroleum]] reserves at Teapot Dome in [[Wyoming]] and in [[California]], set aside by President [[William Howard Taft]]. Leases were awarded without competitive bidding in 1922. Fall became the first presidential cabinet member to go to prison, but no one was convicted of paying the bribes. Congress responded by granting itself permanent subpoena power over tax records. Before [[Watergate scandal|Watergate]], it was called the "greatest and most sensational scandal in the history of American politics."

Synthetic [[Chemical element|chemical element]] with symbol Tc and atomic number 43. It is the lightest element whose isotopes are all radioactive, and one of only two radioactive elements flanked by elements with stable forms, the other being promethium. Naturally occurring traces arise as a spontaneous fission product in [[Uranium|uranium]] and [[Thorium|thorium]] ores. [[Dmitri Mendeleev]] predicted its properties, calling the gap in his periodic table ekamanganese. In 1937 it became the first predominantly artificial element to be produced; its name comes from the Greek for "artificial." Technetium-99m is used in nuclear medicine, for example in bone cancer diagnoses. Commercial isotopes are byproducts of uranium-235 fission in [[Nuclear reactor|nuclear reactors]]. In 1952, its detection in [[Red giant|red giants]] helped show that stars can produce heavier elements.

Discipline of making drawings that visually communicate how something functions or is constructed. Technical drawing is essential in [[Engineering|engineering]] and industry. Its conventions, including [[Symbol|symbols]], perspectives, units of measurement and notation systems, form a visual language intended to have one meaning, unlike artistic drawings in the [[Visual arts|visual arts]]. Many of its principles are codified in the international standard ISO 128. Traditional drafting used a drawing board, a sliding T-square and triangles to draw parallel and angled lines, with compasses and French curves for arcs and curves. Templates allow common symbols to be reused, as in [[Stagecraft|stagecraft]], where lighting designers draw from a standard library of fixture symbols. Since the late 20th century, computer-aided design (CAD) software has revolutionized the field.

Branch of [[Geography|geography]] concerned with tools and techniques for obtaining, analyzing and communicating spatial information. Technical geographers often write their own software and adapt methods across fields, such as kriging, developed for mining and later applied to real estate appraisal. The discipline works mostly with quantitative data and is theoretically grounded in [[Information theory|information theory]]. Core concepts include autocorrelation, a statistical measure of how similar observations are across time or distance, and [[Cartography|cartographic]] generalization, which helps reveal patterns in data. Its subbranches are geographic information science, geomatics and geoinformatics. Key tools include [[Geographic information system|geographic information systems]] and [[Remote sensing|remote sensing]]. The Information Age pushed development of techniques for handling spatial data.

Hypothetical event in which technological growth accelerates beyond human control. In I. J. Good's 1965 "intelligence explosion" model, an upgradable intelligent agent enters a feedback loop of self-improvement, producing superintelligence far beyond human intelligence. [[John von Neumann]] was the first person known to discuss a "singularity" in technological progress. Critics including [[Paul Allen]], Gordon Moore and Roger Penrose argue that [[Artificial intelligence|artificial intelligence]] growth will run into diminishing returns. Stuart J. Russell and Peter Norvig note that improvement in a given area typically follows an S curve, accelerating and then leveling off.

Shawnee chief and warrior who resisted U.S. expansion onto Native American lands. Born in what is now [[Ohio]], he fought in the border conflicts that cost the Shawnees their territory. In 1808 he and his brother Tenskwatawa established Prophetstown, a multi-tribal village in present-day [[Indiana]]. Tecumseh argued that tribal lands were owned in common and should not be ceded unless all agreed. After American forces defeated Tenskwatawa at the Battle of Tippecanoe, Tecumseh allied with the British in the [[War of 1812]], and his warriors helped capture [[Detroit]]. He was killed at the Battle of the Thames, after which his confederacy collapsed. He became a folk hero in American, Indigenous and Canadian history, though mythology has obscured many details of his life.

American serial killer who kidnapped, raped and murdered dozens of young women and girls between 1974 and 1978. He lured victims by feigning injury or posing as an authority figure, then bludgeoned and restrained them, often driving them away in a [[Volkswagen Beetle]]. Arrested in Utah in 1975 for kidnapping, he escaped custody twice while facing murder charges in Colorado. In Florida he committed further murders before his recapture in 1978. He was executed in the [[Electric chair|electric chair]] at Florida State Prison. Biographer Ann Rule called him "a sadistic sociopath."

American actor and producer, known for playing Sam Malone in the NBC sitcom *Cheers*. He won two Primetime Emmy Awards and two Golden Globe Awards for that role. His films include *Three Men and a Baby* (1987) and *Saving Private Ryan* (1998). Later roles include the CBS drama *CSI: Crime Scene Investigation* and the HBO comedy *Curb Your Enthusiasm*. He has been married to actress [[Mary Steenburgen]] since 1995. Danson has campaigned for ocean conservation since the 1980s, co-founding the American Oceans Campaign and serving as vice chairman of Oceana.

American mathematician and domestic [[Terrorism|terrorist]], known as the Unabomber. A mathematics prodigy, he abandoned academic life for a remote cabin near Lincoln, Montana, and waged a mail bombing campaign against people he believed were advancing modern [[Technology|technology]] and environmental destruction. His bombings killed three people and injured 23 others between 1978 and 1995. In 1995 his manifesto, *Industrial Society and Its Future*, was published in [[The Washington Post]] after he promised to stop if a major newspaper printed it. His brother recognized the prose style and alerted the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]]. He pleaded guilty in 1998 and received life sentences without parole.

American lawyer and politician, a [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] senator from [[Massachusetts]] from 1962 until his death. The younger brother of [[John F. Kennedy]] and [[Robert F. Kennedy]], he was known for his oratory and for major laws, including the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. He championed universal health care and was unabashedly liberal. In 1969 his car went off a bridge at Chappaquiddick Island, killing passenger Mary Jo Kopechne; he pleaded guilty to leaving the scene of an accident. The incident hindered his presidential ambitions, and he lost the 1980 Democratic nomination to [[Jimmy Carter]].

American media proprietor and philanthropist, founder of [[CNN]], the first 24-hour cable news channel. He took over his father's billboard business in 1963 and in 1970 bought an [[Atlanta]] UHF station, beginning what became the Turner Broadcasting System. His company founded WTBS, a pioneering cable superstation. Turner owned the Atlanta Braves, which won the 1995 [[World Series]], and in 1988 he bought Jim Crockett Promotions, rebranding it WCW. He gave $1 billion to create the United Nations Foundation and co-founded the Nuclear Threat Initiative with Sam Nunn in 2001. [[Forbes]] gave him a perfect philanthropy score in 2020. He amassed the largest privately owned bison herd in the world and was the largest private landowner in the United States until 2011.

American media franchise about four anthropomorphic turtle brothers trained in ninjutsu who fight evil in New York City. Created by comic artists Kevin Eastman and Peter Laird as a parody of superhero comics, it features Leonardo, [[Donatello]], [[Raphael]] and [[Michelangelo]]. The first comic was published in 1984 by Mirage Studios. Licensing to Playmates Toys produced [[Action figure|action figures]] worth about $1.1 billion between 1988 and 1992. The first film, released in 1990, became the highest-grossing independent film up to that point. The franchise has since spanned television series, films and video games, including the 2023 animated film *Mutant Mayhem*.

Small black leather boxes with straps, containing parchment scrolls inscribed with Torah verses. Traditionally worn by adult [[Jews|Jewish]] men on weekday mornings during prayer, the arm and head tefillin are bound to the arm and placed on the forehead. In [[Orthodox Judaism|Orthodox]] communities only men wear them, and [[Halakha|Jewish law]] generally exempts women. Tefillin fulfill Torah instructions to keep a sign of the Exodus from [[Egypt]]. Archaeological finds at Qumran show that Jews wore some form of tefillin by the 1st century CE, and the [[New Testament]] also refers to them.

Capital and largest city of [[Honduras]], with its sister city Comayagüela. Spanish settlers claimed the site in 1578. It became the national capital in 1880, when President Marco Aurelio Soto moved the seat of government from Comayagua. The two sister cities form a Central District that serves as the permanent national capital, and the city hosts 25 foreign embassies and the country's most important public university. Its infrastructure has not kept pace with population growth, and roads struggle to handle more than 400,000 vehicles. The economy relies on government services, [[Commerce|commerce]], light manufacturing such as [[Textile|textiles]] and food processing, and remittances from abroad. Gang activity and [[Organized crime|organized crime]] have driven high homicide rates.

Capital and largest city of [[Iran]], at the southern foothills of the Alborz Mountains. Tehran has about 9 million residents in the city and 16.8 million in its metropolitan area, making it the most populous city in Iran and [[West Asia]]. Agha Mohammad Khan of the Qajar dynasty made it the capital in 1786, partly for its proximity to the [[Caucasus]]. Under Reza Shah it gained Iran's first institute of higher learning, bank and railway line. The city was central to the [[Iranian Revolution]] and suffered bombing during the [[Iran–Iraq War]]. Its Golestan Palace is a [[World Heritage Site]], and the Milad Tower is the world's sixth-tallest self-supporting tower. Air pollution, earthquakes and water scarcity have prompted plans to relocate the capital, though none has been approved.

Mediterranean coastal city in central [[Israel]], the economic and technological center of the country. Officially Tel Aviv-Yafo, it is the most populous city in the Gush Dan metropolitan area and home to most of Israel's foreign embassies. The city was founded in 1909 as *Ahuzat Bayit*, a Jewish housing estate on the outskirts of the ancient port of Jaffa, then part of the [[Ottoman Empire]]. Its name was taken from [[Theodor Herzl]]'s 1902 novel *Altneuland*. In 1948 Israel's Declaration of Independence was proclaimed in the city. Its White City, with the world's largest concentration of International Style buildings, including [[Bauhaus]] architecture, has been a [[World Heritage Site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]] since 2003. Tel Aviv University, the country's largest, has more than 30,000 students.

State in southern [[India]] on the Deccan Plateau. Formed in 2014 after decades of protest, it corresponds to the Telugu-speaking regions of the former princely state of [[Hyderabad]], which is its capital and largest city and a major center for information technology. Telugu is the main official language, and Urdu has second official status. Earlier rulers included the [[Satavahana dynasty]], which traded as far as the [[Roman Empire]], and the Kakatiyas, whose Ramappa Temple is a [[World Heritage Site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]]. The state is an important base for Indian defense and research laboratories.

Cloud-based, cross-platform [[Social media|social media]] and instant messaging service, founded in 2013 by brothers Pavel and Nikolai Durov. Its headquarters are in [[Dubai]], United Arab Emirates. Users exchange messages and media, and groups can hold up to 200,000 members. Channels allow one-way broadcasts to unlimited audiences. End-to-end encryption covers voice and video calls, and optionally private chats. Telegram runs on [[Android (operating system)|Android]], [[IOS|iOS]], [[Linux]] and [[Web browser|web browsers]]. As of March 2025 it had more than 1 billion monthly active users, most of them in India. Governments in Russia, Iran and Brazil have banned or restricted it.

Long-distance transmission of messages using symbolic codes known to sender and recipient, rather than a physical exchange of objects. The earliest true telegraph in wide use was the optical Chappe telegraph, invented by Claude Chappe in the late 18th century and used extensively in France during the Napoleonic era. Electric telegraphs began replacing optical systems in the mid-19th century. The [[Samuel Morse|Morse]] system, developed in the United States, became the international standard in 1865, using a modified code developed in Germany. Heliographs, which used reflected sunlight, were standard military equipment as late as [[World War II]]. Telegrams became popular once prices fell, but the [[Telephone|telephone]] drove the telegraph into decline from 1920 onward.

Automatic collection and transmission of measurements from remote points to receiving equipment for monitoring. The word derives from Greek roots meaning "far off" and "measure." Telemetry systems use [[Radio|radio]], infrared or wired links, and many send data by [[SMS]] over GSM networks. A telemeter consists of a sensor, a transmission path and a display, recording or control device. Radio telemetry became routine as space exploration began, and the German [[V-2 rocket|V-2 rocket]] program used it during [[World War II]]. Today telemetry monitors [[Spacecraft|spacecraft]], patients' vital signs and wildlife movements.
